attrs.evidence: lowering_check.mjs 13/13, the first end-to-end witness: add(const 2, const 3) with inputs={} lowers to one canonical ic32 term whose identity the kernel and ic32_canon agree on; the host launches the catalogued binary and observes the canonical normal form L0(L1(A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,A(N0,N1))))))); that decodes structurally to {status:'value', value:5}; and its outcome id EQUALS the source evaluator's, whose result was itself accepted by an authority owning every oracle it consulted (derivation.acceptance-authority@1). six-identities-stay-distinct asserts all six values differ. native-film-absent-by-refusal asserts the film emitter REFUSES this exact fixture with film-dup-cell-present — the gap is measured at the fixture the refinement runs on rather than described in the abstract. At B1.2.1 the anti-collapse case is chain-identities-stay-distinct: it requires a value for every node REFINEMENT_CHAIN marks exercised, fails if a declared node is not wired into the witness, and NAMES the unexercised ones in its output -- a node silently absent and a node declared absent being the difference between a stale instrument and a scoped one. B2: every node of REFINEMENT_CHAIN is now exercised -- the witness reaches native code THROUGH instantiate(), so instantiation_sem_id and inputs_sem_id stopped being declared architecture. B2.1: the chain is ELEVEN nodes, all exercised — closed_template_sem_id and emission_sem_id joined it when the split fired, and the derived anti-collapse set grew with it without anyone editing a count. I-4c is now FILM-EVIDENCED: the x + (x + y) term emits a 12-frame all-APP-LAM film terminating in NORMAL_FORM which the kernel replays on two runtime classes, so the INPUT refinement witness carries the grade the no-input one has had since round 26. This does NOT advance the runtime frontier: every frame is APP-LAM at tree loci, and the six DUP-* rules, the d:/v: loci and BUDGET_EXHAUSTED remain exactly as unexercised.
attrs.statement: SOURCE AND TARGET AGREE ON THE OUTCOME: source_outcome_sem_id == target_outcome_sem_id, where the target side is reached by canonical lowering, native ic32 execution, and structural decoding. TWO GRADES OF EVIDENCE FOR THE EXECUTION LEG, and only the first is claimed here. OBSERVED: the ObservedExecutionHost hashed a catalogued binary and then ran it, so the normal form is an execution event the host drove (derivation.implementation-provenance@4). FILM-EVIDENCED: the transition sequence itself is replayed by the independent kernel (film.native-emission@1). BOTH ARE NOW CLAIMED for the first witness: ic32_film v0.2.0 emits six chained APP-LAM frames for the lowered term and the kernel replays the chain. Round 25 recorded the second as OPEN on the strength of a refusal that was right about the fixture and wrong about its reason — the lowered term carries dup cells and fires none. What remains OPEN is a fixture where a DUP-* rule actually becomes enabled -- CLOSED AT B3.2 BY film.native-emission@2, AND NOT BY THIS FIXTURE, which is the distinction worth keeping: the lowered add still fires no dup rule and still emits the same six APP-LAM frames, so what changed is the EMITTER's reach and not this witness's coverage. At v0.2.0 those six frames were the limit of what could be filmed; at v0.3.0 they are a fact about the term. A refinement witness whose grade improves because a neighbouring capability grew, without its own fixture exercising the new capability, has not gained evidence -- and saying so is the only thing that keeps the two apart. Reporting the two grades separately is the point: an execution the host observed and an execution the kernel replayed are different claims. THIS IS THE THEOREM; canonical-lowering@1 and target-decoding@1 exist to make it DIAGNOSABLE, because a bare equality failure cannot say which of three relations broke. THE CHAIN'S IDENTITIES STAY DISTINCT AND NONE MAY BE COLLAPSED INTO ANOTHER, and the chain is DECLARED rather than counted in prose: program_sem_id, lowering_sem_id, target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id, target_nf_sem_id, decode_sem_id, outcome_sem_id, of which the last two of the first five are DECLARED AND NOT EXERCISED until instantiation is built. THIS SENTENCE SAID 'SIX' AND OMITTED target_template_sem_id for the whole of B1.2, the pass that introduced it as an independently identified semantic object -- so the law, and the anti-collapse witness reading it, made a six-way claim about a seven-node chain and were green throughout. The enumeration now lives in REFINEMENT_CHAIN with an exercised flag per node and the witness DERIVES its set from it, because a hand-typed count drifting from the thing it counts is a species this tree has now caught in a law count, a case count, a rung count and here. Collapsing any pair turns a refinement statement into a renaming, which is the failure mode this whole chain is built to avoid. BUILT AT B2, AND BUILDING IT MOVED NEITHER SEMANTIC ID -- the property B1.1 split the records to make possible and the first round able to exercise it. `input` lowers to a structural port, instantiate() closes a template against canonical inputs, both lifecycle flags are true and all three port falsifiers are WITNESSED; none of that moved lsem or isem, and the measurement is an EQUATION rather than a simulation: put back only op_lowering_rules and only emission and the B1.2.1 identities return EXACTLY, so those two fields are the only hashed bytes the round touched. THE SOURCE-TO-TEMPLATE MAP IS STRUCTURAL AND INTERPRETED: lower() reads op_lowering_rules rather than carrying a second hand-coded copy of it, so a rule cannot be edited without changing behaviour and behaviour cannot change without moving LOWERING_SEM_ID. English rules beside a hand-coded implementation are two artifacts that can disagree while only one is hashed -- the codomain-in-prose defect one layer in -- and `transform: identity` on the port's source name is the no-normalization ruling made structural rather than stated. LOWER() NO LONGER RETURNS AN EXECUTABLE TERM. The convenience field was a SECOND PATH: the official route through instantiate() beside a shortcut through lowering, with every future reader having to remember which carried the semantics, which is how a hidden second mechanism returns. It is removed and the equality survives as a REGRESSION THEOREM -- instantiate(template, {}) reproduces the exact 129 bytes, the same six-frame film, the same normal form and the same 5. AND instantiate() MAY NOT MINT THE IDENTITY OF ITS OWN OUTPUT: an instantiator that emitted bytes and certified their semantic id would produce the artifact and the certificate from one source, so a wrong emission would carry a matching id and verify against itself. The kernel canonicalises the bytes; the receipt is built around that id; verification RE-INSTANTIATES and RE-CANONICALISES independently rather than asking the instantiator to agree with itself. THE EMISSION SPLIT TRIGGER MOVED TO STATUS and gained two conditions: split emission into its own relation when it becomes independently REUSED, independently THEOREM-BEARING, independently VERSIONED OR REPLACEABLE, or when the closed-template intermediate becomes an independently IDENTIFIED or EXTERNALLY OBSERVED artifact. The last two fire first -- the moment two emitters are compared over one closed template, an emitter upgrade re-cutting the semantic identity of PORT SUBSTITUTION is plainly wrong. Keeping that trigger inside the hashed semantics, as B1.2.1 did, re-committed B1.1's own finding: governance prose inside a relation identity re-identifies the relation when it is reworded. STILL DECLARED OPEN: source-refusal to instantiation-refusal preservation, unchanged. CORRECTED AND SPLIT AT B2.1. THREE THINGS, AND THE FIRST IS A DEFECT. (1) THE INSTANTIATOR MAY NOT READ ITS ARGUMENTS TWICE. B2's instantiate() read the caller's inputs once to BIND values into the term and again to compute inputs_sem_id, so a getter answering 2 and then 999 produced a term meaning x=2 beside an identity committing to {x:999} -- an application record asserting 'these inputs were {x:999}' above 'this term represents x=2'. Nothing about the runtime was wrong: the RELATION misbound its own input identity. That is derivation.entry-snapshot@1 arriving in the compiler layer, and the repair is the same mechanism: ONE canonical snapshot of BOTH arguments at entry, everything downstream reading the snapshot. THE INVARIANT: the bytes inputs_sem_id identifies are exactly the bytes from which every substituted value was derived. (2) A CLOSED VOCABULARY OF BARE NAMES STILL HIDES SEMANTICS. B2's rule table named predicates and transforms and bound each name to a JavaScript function, so redefining `integer` from Number.isInteger to always-true made const(1.5) lower successfully instead of refusing WITH LOWERING_SEM_ID UNCHANGED, and `identity` could have been made to normalize a source input name, silently undoing the port ruling. The vocabulary stays CLOSED and its DEFINITIONS are now data hashed into the relation; a rule may not name a predicate by JavaScript reference or by a bare string resolved elsewhere, and when the core exports reusable semantic predicates a rule references one by its predicate_sem_id. The kind interpreter is trusted code like canonicalBytes: what has been removed is the rule LANGUAGE's ability to hide meaning. (3) THE EMISSION SPLIT TRIGGER FIRED, AND B2 TRIPPED ALL FOUR CONDITIONS AT ONCE. emit() is exported and independently reused; I-4a is a theorem about EMISSION ALONE, comparing two emitters over one template; the executable encoding carries its own content identity and an alternate emitter was deliberately run against it; and instantiate() RETURNED the closed template to its caller. The condition that settles it is the second: once two emitters are compared over one closed template, an emitter upgrade re-cutting the semantic identity of PORT SUBSTITUTION is plainly wrong, which is exactly what a merged relation does. So INSTANTIATION ENDS AT A CLOSED TEMPLATE and EMISSION is a third relation with EMISSION_SEM_ID: program -(lowering)-> template -(instantiation + inputs)-> CLOSED TEMPLATE -(emission)-> target term -(native film)-> normal form -(decode)-> outcome. The closed template carries its OWN IDENTITY DOMAIN, ctmpl- against tmpl-, EVEN WHERE ITS BYTES EQUAL AN OPEN TEMPLATE'S: for a program with no inputs the two structures are byte-identical and they are not the same thing -- one is what the COMPILER produced and the other is what an INVOCATION closed, and sharing an id would make 'this was instantiated' and 'this needed no instantiation' indistinguishable. Two receipts, each verified by recomputation of its OWN relation and neither filmed: InstantiationReceipt {target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, closed_template_sem_id} and EmissionReceipt {closed_template_sem_id, emission_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}. THE SPLIT MADE THE VERIFIERS CLEANER, which is an argument for it rather than a consequence: verifying instantiation needs NO runtime canonicaliser at all, because the relation now ends at a structure the module owns, and only emission needs one -- which it TAKES AS A PARAMETER, because the module that defines a relation must not also choose the oracle that judges it. Both verifiers are production functions; at B2 the only implementation of 'does this receipt hold?' lived in the test suite, and a relation whose verification procedure exists only in its own tests is a relation nobody else can check.
